subject: Post-call: edge locations & hyperscaler comparison — next tests and timeline
messages:
From: Oliver James <oliver.james@edgebank.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>; ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeBank IT <it@edgebank.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: initial call — edge locations and perf overview

Thanks for the walkthrough today — useful session. Attached is a short internal latency dump from two of our branch regions (Mid-Atlantic, Pacific Northwest) that illustrates the client-perceived P95s hitting their routing layer. (attachment: edgebank_latency_report.csv, CSV, ~38KB).

A few takeaways from our side:
- We currently route to a central inference endpoint in us-east-1; some customers are seeing 120-180ms tail when combined with our app layer.
- Compliance team flagged potential data residency constraints for a subset of records that must remain in US-owned datacenters.
- We're also evaluating managed endpoints from HyperscalerA and HyperscalerB; their public SLA is attractive but the observed multi-region consistency is unclear.

Next asks from us: can Redwood show a short comparison that contrasts (a) multi-region P99 across edge locations, (b) cold-start tail, and (c) any caching/KV strategies that would reduce apparent client latency? Ideally something we can share with our infra lead by Tuesday.

Oliver
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeBank
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@edgebank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-22T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: initial call — edge locations and perf overview

Thanks Oliver — appreciate the quick notes and the CSV. We will own the comparison and propose a concrete test matrix. High-level response from the call:

1) What Redwood brings vs the hyperscalers you mentioned
- Smart routing: we can pin inference to region-local GPU pools or route by latency policy; this reduces RTT compared to a single central endpoint.
- KV prefix caching + local hot-shard: for repeated prompt prefixes we can serve from local caches (reduces token generation latency for interactive flows).
- Quantization-aware kernels: same model variants but tuned per-hardware for consistent tail latency across regions.
- Data residency controls: our Private mode lets you restrict inference to US-only hosts and provides KMS integrations for keys.

2) Proposed quick tests (we'll run and provide CSV + charts):
- P50/P95/P99 token-response latency from three customer-facing edge locations (us-east, us-west, us-central) against: Redwood-hosted (region-local), HyperscalerA managed endpoint (their closest region), and HyperscalerB.
- Cold-start measurement: aggregate cold-start latency over 100 cold calls per region.
- Cache-hit delta: synthetic workload with 30% repeated prefixes to show savings with prefix caching.
- Throughput under realistic burst: 10k concurrent small (<=64-token) requests for 120s.

3) Timeline / access
- We can run an initial run by Monday (2027-03-24) if you can grant a temporary test token and allow 3 egress endpoints (us-east, us-west, us-central).
- Marissa will own the benchmark runs; Ben will attach the kernel/quantization notes for the models we test.

I've attached a short comparison PDF summarizing kernel differences we plan to run. (attachment: redwood-arm-compare.pdf)

I'll loop back with the test matrix in a follow-up. Thanks — excited to show where we can tighten tails.

— Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>; ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>; stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver James <oliver.james@edgebank.com>
Date: 2027-03-23T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: initial call — edge locations and perf overview

Internal notes / test plan (will post results to the shared Drive folder above):

Quick plan details — non-exhaustive:
- Models: we will test the same open family you mentioned on the call (v3-family-4b quant / int8 and an fp16 baseline).
- Regions & endpoints: us-east-1 (N. Virginia), us-west-2 (Oregon), us-central-1 (Chicago). Each run will record: request timestamp, local server enqueue-to-send, model-infer-time, and total client-observed RTT.
- Measurement specifics:
  * P50 / P95 / P99 (token-level response completion)
  * Cold-starts: ensure clean cache + cold container spin-up for 100 unique instances
  * Cache experiment: synthetic corpus with 30% prefix repetition; we'll report hit rate and token-latency delta
  * KV-residency test: we will demonstrate local KV scoping (requests pinned to US-only stores) to show compliance behavior
- Deliverables: CSV (per-run), charts (latency percentiles), short notes on config used (batching, concurrency, quant settings).

Dependencies / asks from EdgeBank:
- Temporary test API key allowing requests from our test workers IPs (we can share IPs once you approve)
- Confirmation that PII/data types in test payloads are permitted; if not, we will use synthetic sanitized data

I attached a proposed test matrix to this thread (proposed-test-matrix.xlsx) and will start scheduling runs once we have the test key.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Oliver James <oliver.james@edgebank.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, EdgeBank IT <it@edgebank.com>
Date: 2027-03-24T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: initial call — edge locations and perf overview

Thanks Karthik & Marissa — this is exactly what we were hoping for.

We can provide a temporary API key scoped to a testing project and allow the Redwood test worker IPs (I put the IP approval on our infra lead's plate today). We'll validate synthetic payloads only for the first run; if all good we can allow a small subset of production-like fixtures next week.

Please proceed with the Monday run. Two small clarifications:
- Can you include the Hyperscaler vendors' endpoint config you test (region + instance class) so we can map apples-to-apples capacity?
- For data-residency proof points, can you provide the KMS/HSM control names and any attestations we can include in our compliance notebook?

If you can share the initial CSV + charts to the Drive link you listed, I'll route to our infra and compliance teams.

Oliver
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeBank
